1 1.

The petitioner filed this petition under Section 164 of Motor Vehicles Act 1989, seeking compensation of Rs.2,50,000/- for the injures sustained by him in the road traffic accident occurred on 26.12.2022.
2.

It is the case of the petitioner that, on 26.12.2022 at about 9.20 p.m., within the jurisdiction of Kumaraswamy Layout Traffic Police Station, near Gowdanapalya Bus stop, when the driver of the unoffending BMTC Bus bearing Reg. No.KA-53-F-0233 drove the same from Kadirenahalli towards Uttarahalli, at that time the Petitioner / accused drove the offending Motor Cycle bearing Reg.
No.KA-03-HR-2647 from Uttarahalli towards Kadirenahalli in a high speed, rash or negligent manner so as to endangering human life and came in the right side of the road and dashed against the unoffending vehicle, as a result the accused/ Petitioner has sustained grievous injuries.

Further it is alleged that at the time of accident the accused was not wearing helmet and the said offending M.V.C.No.4003/2023 3 SCCH - 7 vehicle is not duly insured and the RC owner of the offending vehicle has given the said uninsured offending vehicle to the accused/ Petitioner to ride.
Thereafter Petitioner was shifted to Hill side Hospital and for higher treatment he was shifted to Sagar Hospital, Bengaluru for higher treatment.
Thereafter, informant/ Kruthi. M. given complaint before the Kumaraswamy Layout Traffic police Station.

Accordingly, a case was registered in their Crime No.280/2022 and prepared F.I.R. for the offence punishable under sections 279 of IPC R/w section 129 R/w Sec. 177, Section 146 R/w Sec.196 of MV Act and submitted to the jurisdictional judicial magistrate and the superior officers and investigation was taken up by the investigating Officer.

Further it is alleged that prior to the alleged accident the Petitioner was hale and healthy and he was aged about 25 years and he was working as a Driver and earning an income of Rs.8,000/- per month.
Due to the injuries sustained in the alleged accident he became permanently disabled and he is unable to do his work normally as he was doing prior to the occurrence of the alleged accident.

The alleged accident is occurred due to fault and negligence act of the driver of the unoffending BMTC Bus bearing Reg.No.KA-53-F-0233 and Respondent is M.V.C.No.4003/2023 4 SCCH - 7 the owner of the unoffending vehicle, as such the respondent is liable to pay compensation to Petitioner.
Hence Petitioner filed the present claim petition for seeking compensation.

3. In response to the notice, the respondent has appeared through their counsel and filed their written statement by admitting the ownership of the unoffending BMTC bus bearing registration No.KA-53-F-0233 and by denying the petition averments and contended that, alleged accident occurred due to negligence and fault on the part of the petitioner himself and there is no such negligence or fault on the part of the driver of the said unoffending BMTC Bus and therefore the Charge Sheet is rightly filed against the Petitioner/accused, as such Respondent is not liable to pay any compensation to the petitioner.
Further it is denied the age, income and occupation of the deceased and expenses incurred towards medication and other charges as alleged.

Further respondent contended that, the compensation claimed by the Petitioner is highly excessive,
exorbitant and imaginary.
Hence, on all these grounds, the respondent prayed for dismissal of claim petition.
4. On the basis of above pleadings following Issues were framed.

No.KA-53-F-0233 drove the same from Kadirenahalli towards Uttarahalli, at that time the Petitioner / accused drove the offending Motor Cycle bearing Reg. Further it is alleged that at the time of accident the accused was not wearing helmet and the said offending vehicle is not duly insured and the RC owner of the offending vehicle has given the said uninsured offending vehicle to the accused/ Petitioner to ride.

It is contended that the accident was occurred due to involvement of the both vehicles.

The Respondent admitted the alleged accident and its version is that, the alleged accident occurred due to the negligence and fault of the rider of the offending vehicle and no fault of the driver of the unoffending vehicle and therefore the driver of the unoffending vehicle cannot be held to be negligent and therefore the police have rightly filed Charge Sheet against the rider/ accused/ Petitioner of the offending vehicle.
As such the Respondent is not liable to pay any compensation and in order to obtained compensation the Petitioner has constrained to filed the present claim petition.

Further it is denied that the age, income and occupation of the Petitioner and the petition is false and frivolous in the eye of law and the quantum of compensation claimed by the claimant is exorbitant and sought for dismissal of the petition.
10.
The burden to prove the framed issues lies on the Petitioner.

Hence, in order to prove his case,
the Petitioner himself examined as P.W.1 and he has reiterated the entire petition averments and contentions taken in the course of claim petition in his evidence before this Court and also produced as many as Exs.P.1 M.V.C.No.4003/2023 8 SCCH - 7 to P.10 documents.
Therefore, there is no necessity to repeat those facts again.
I have gone through the documents produced by the PW-1.

Ex.P-1 is the True copy of FIR, Ex.P-2 is the True copy of complaint, Ex.P.3 is the Spot Mahazar,
Ex.P.4 is the Motor Vehicle Accident report, Ex.P-5 is the Wound Certificate, Ex.P.6 is the true copy of Charge sheet, Ex.P.7 and 8 are the Discharge summaries, Ex.P.9 is the Hospital and Medicine bill and Ex.P.10 is the driving licence of the petitioner.
11.
In the cross-examination of PW-1 by Respondent, he has deposed that the RC owner of the offending Motor Cycle is Sri. Armugam.
Further he has denied that at the time of accident he is not possessing valid and effective driving licence to ride the offending vehicle and the said vehicle is not duly insured.
Further he has denied that at the time of accident he was not wearing helmet.
Further he has denied that the alleged accident occurred due to his negligence and fault and no fault of the driver of the unoffending vehicle.
Further he has deposed that he do not know whether the offending vehicle is duly insured at the time of accident.

Further he has denied that at the time of accident he drove the offending vehicle in wrong direction and due to his fault M.V.C.No.4003/2023 9 SCCH - 7 he dashed against the unoffending vehicle and caused the alleged accident.
Further he has denied that he is hale and healthy and he is doing work and other regular activities as past.
Further he has deposed that he is working as a driver and earning income of Rs.8,000/- p.m., and in this regard he has not produced any documents to show his income.
Further he has denied that he has not incurred Rs.1,00,000/- towards his medical expenditure.
Further he has denied that in order to get more compensation he has produced concocted created documents and filed false evidence affidavit and deposing falsely and he is deposing falsely.
During the cross, examination Pw.1 has consistently deposed on the lines of the petition/prosecution case and he has made those versions, which could not be shattered in cross examination.

12. In order to prove the version of Respondent, the Respondent has examined the driver of the offending vehicle as RW-1 and he has reiterated the entire written statement averments and contentions taken in the course of written statement in his evidence before this Court.

Therefore,
there is no necessity to repeat those facts again.

Further he has denied that the alleged accident occurred due to his negligence and fault and no fault of the rider of the offending vehicle.
Further he has deposed that he has lodged the complaint regarding to alleged accident.

Further he has denied that in order to escape from the liability, in collusion with the police he has falsely implicated the rider of the offending vehicle and filed false complaint and filed false evidence affidavit and deposing falsely.

13. On careful reading of Ex.P4/IMV report it specifies that the Motor Vehicle Inspector has been clearly opined that, the said incident did not occur because of the mechanical defects in respect of the said offending and unoffending vehicle.
Further the said Inspector noticed the damages to the unoffending vehicle and opined that, front bumper on right hand side is broken and damaged and front right side corner mouffsil body is damaged.

Further the said Inspector noticed the damages to the offending vehicle and opined that, Front mudguard is broken and damaged, front shock absorber is bent and damaged, Head light assembly is broken and damaged, Handle bent, Head light mask cover is broken, Odometer M.V.C.No.4003/2023 11 SCCH - 7 Assembly is broken and front left hand and right hand side indicator assembly is broken and damaged.
14.
On going through the Ex.P-6/Wound Certificate it is seen that the Doctor opined that the Petitioner was admitted to the Sagar Hospital, Bengaluru.

In the alleged accident the Petitioner has sustained Laceration over left eye brow, Abrasion and swelling over right leg- below knee-Tibia fracture, Left ear bleeding present, Right eye lid swollen (upper eye lid)-Facial bone fracture and Abrasions over left side of abdomen and right foot.
Further the doctor opined that the injuries No.1 to 4 are grievous in nature and injury No.5 is simple in nature.

16. On going through the Ex.P3/spot Mahazar it is seen that in pursuance of the alleged Ex.P2/statement, on 27.12.2022 the police have came to the spot and informant Kirthi M showed the spot to the police and the police were conducted the detailed spot mahazar in the presence of panch witnesses.
17. Admittedly, the accused/ Petitioner is the rider of the offending vehicle and further admitted that, Petitioner sustained grievous injuries due to alleged accident.

The counsel for Respondent claimed the said driver of the unoffending vehicle to be innocent and further the counsel for Respondent contended that, the alleged accident occurred due to negligence and fault of the rider of the offending vehicle and no fault of the driver of the unoffending Bus, slowly he may be driving and therefore he cannot be held to be negligent and therefore the police have rightly filed Charge Sheet against the Petitioner.

. On going through the prosecution papers, FIR, Spot Mahazar, MVA Report, Wound Certificate,
Charge Sheet, and the evidence of PW-1 and RW-1 is specific to the effect that, the rider of the offending vehicle/accused is the reason for the said incident and at his instance, the incident took place.
The alleged accident was occurred due to rash and negligent riding of the offending vehicle and fault of the accused.

Therefore, considering the above discussed aspects collectively, it is the considered opinion of the Court that, the incident having been taken place in the manner asserted by the prosecution and the same being proved to have been taken place in the manner alleged by the prosecution, the accused drove the offending vehicle in a rash or negligent manner so as to endanger human life and at the spot dashed to the unoffending vehicle, as a result accused/ rider/Petitioner of the offending vehicle sustained grievous injuries in the alleged accident.

The evidence of Pw.1,
RW-1, Ex.P-1/FIR, Ex.P-2/Complaint, Ex.P3/Spot Mahazar, Ex.P4/MVA Report, Ex.P-5/Wound Certificate, Ex.P-6/Charge Sheet, clearly establishes that the alleged accident occurred at the spot.
It is not in dispute as to the aspect that, the Petitioner sustained grievous injuries in the alleged incident.
Because, for the above M.V.C.No.4003/2023 15 SCCH - 7 reasons collectively it is clear that, the accident happened due to rash or negligent act of the accused.
It is evident that injuries noted in the Ex.P5/Wound Certificate would be caused by a road traffic accident.

At the same time,
it has come out in evidence that the alleged accident was occurred due to rash and negligent riding of the offending vehicle and fault of the accused/rider.
Matters being so, the acts of the accused person clearly constitute the offences punishable under sections 279 of IPC R/w section 129 R/w Sec. 177, Section 146 R/w Sec.196 of MV Act.

Thus because of such negligent act of the accused/rider of the offending vehicle, it resulted in the injuries to himself, as the accused drove the said offending vehicle very rashly and negligently on the spot.
Therefore, the alleged accident occurred due to the fault of the accused/rider of the offending vehicle.

In this matter the alleged accident occurred due Dharanraj vs B.M.T.C on 8 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/112242500/

sentences.text: Accordingly I answered Issue No.1 in the Affirmative.
19. Issue No.2:-
The Learned counsel for the Petitioner has contended that the injured Petitioner was aged about 25 years and he was working as a Driver and earning an income of Rs.8,000/- per month.

As such the Petitioner M.V.C.No.4003/2023 16 SCCH - 7 is entitled for compensation under the head of pain and suffering, mental agony, medical expenses, special diet, conveyance, loss of future income due to disability, loss of amenities and loss of income during laid up period and prays to award the compensation as prayed in the petition.

20. On the other hand, the learned counsel for Respondent contended that even though the Petitioner claimed that his earning was about Rs.8,000/- per month, the same is not established by the claimant by producing the documents.

In this matter the alleged accident occurred due to negligence and fault of the Petitioner / accused / rider of the offending vehicle and no fault of the driver of the unoffending vehicle and therefore no risk is contemplated under the insurance policy in respect of self negligence accident and therefore denied the factum of claim and since the Petitioner has not established her income, he is not entitled for compensation towards such prospects and hence prays dismissal of the petition.

21. The petitioner contended that as on the date of the accident he was aged about 25 years and he relied on the Ex.P.10/Driving licence of the Petitioner and wherein the date of birth of the Petitioner is shown as M.V.C.No.4003/2023 17 SCCH - 7 03.06.1997 and this accident was occurred on 26.12.2022.
Hence it is clear that on the strength of the Ex.P-10/ Driving licence as on the date of the accident the Petitioner was aged about 25 years and 6 months.
Hence the age of the Petitioner is considered as 25 years.
22. It is not in dispute that the Petitioner sustained injuries in the road traffic accident occurred in the alleged accident arising from motor vehicles.

The counsel for the Petitioner contended that in view of the claim petition filed under the provision of the MV Act question of negligence cannot be looked into and counsel for Respondent contended that no risk is contemplated under the insurance policy in respect of self negligent accident.

From the above discussion and going through the provision of the MV Act, it is clear that the grant of compensation under the provision of MV Act with respect to claim petition on the basis of structured formula is in the nature of a final award and the adjudication thereunder is required to be made without any requirement of any proof or negligence of the driver / owner of the vehicle(s) involved in the accident.

In fact as per the claim petition filed under the provision of the MV Act, to permit the insurer to raise the defence M.V.C.No.4003/2023 18 SCCH - 7 of negligence would be to bring a proceeding under 163- A (before amendment) / 164 (after amendment) with effect from 01.04.2022 of the MV Act at par with the proceeding under Section 166 of the Act which would not only be self contradictory but also defeat the very legislative intention.
Hence in view of the claim petition filed under the provision of MV Act the insurer cannot raise any defence or negligence on part of victim to counter a claim for compensation.

Section 164 of MV Act establishes a 'No fault' liability framework for compensation in case of death or grievous hurt resulting from motor vehicle accidents, requiring the owner of the insurer to pay a fixed sum of Rs.5,00,000/- for death and Rs.2,50,000/- for grievous hurt Dharanraj

vs B.M.T.C on 8 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/112242500/
7
irrespective of fault.

23. Chapter 10 of the Motor Vehicle Act, 1988 (prior to 2019 Amendment w.e.f 01.04.2022), the marginal heading of which is "LIABILITY WITHOUT FAULT IN CERTAIN CASES" containing Section 140 to 144 is omitted by Act 32 of 2019 w.e.f. 01.04.2022.
24.
Chapter 11 (containing Sections 145 to 163, 163-A, 163- B and 164) is substituted by the Act 32 of 2019 w.e.f 01.04.2022.

Now as per the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, as amended by the Motor Vehicles (Amendment) Act, 2019 (32 of 2019), Section 164 is introduced, language M.V.C.No.4003/2023 19 SCCH - 7 of which shows that it is a combination of Section 140 and 163-A [prior to 2019 Amendment Act (32 of 2019)].

Section 164 of the Motor Vehicles (Amendment) Act, 2019 (32 of 2019) is reproduced as under:-- Section 164:-- Payment of compensation in case of death or grievous hurt, etc:-- (1) Notwithstanding anything contained in this Act or in any other law for the time being in force or instrument having the force of law, the owner of the motor vehicle or the authorised insurer shall be liable to pay in the case of death or grievous hurt due to any accident arising out of the use of motor vehicle, a compensation, of a sum of five lakh rupees in case of death or of two and a half lakh rupees in case of grievous hurt to the legal heirs or the victim, as the case may be.

( 2 ) In any claim for compensation under sub-section (1), the claimant shall not be required to plead or establish that the death or grievous hurt in respect of which the claim has been made was due to any wrongful act or neglect or default of the owner of the vehicle or of the vehicle concerned or of any other person.

(3) Where, in respect of death or grievous hurt due to an accident arising out of the use of motor vehicle, compensation has been paid under any other law for the M.V.C.No.4003/2023 20 SCCH - 7 time being in force, such amount of compensation shall be reduced from the amount of compensation payable under this section."
25.
OBJECT BEHIND THE LEGISLATION:

There cannot be any dispute that the Motor Vehicles Act is a beneficial piece of legislation and, therefore, endeavour has to be made as to how best the intention of the legislation can be achieved so as to safe-guard the interest of the victims of the accident, rather than defeating the same.
The statute has to be construed according to the intent of the makers and it is the duty of the Courts to interpret the statute in such a manner that the true intention of legislature is achieved.

Taking a purposive interpretation of Section 163-A of the Motor Vehicles Act (pre-amendment i.e 2019 amendment w.e.f 01.04.2022), the clear intention of the legislation was to come to the rescue of all those who in the absence of any evidence are not in a position to file a claim petition under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicle Act, where death of the victim or permanent disablement of the victim is required to be proved by establishing the factum of negligence involving the offending vehicle resulting into causing of accident, but under Section 163-A (pre- Dharanraj vs B.M.T.C on 8 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/112242500/
8 amendment i.e 2019 amendment w.e.f 01.04.2022) the M.V.C.No.4003/2023 21 SCCH - 7

26. A bare reading of Section 164 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (amended by the Act 32 of 2019),
shows that the claimant shall not be required to plead or establish that the death or grievous hurt in respect of which the claim has been made, was due to any wrongful act or neglect or default of the owner of the vehicle or the vehicles concerned or of any other person.
27. The object and purpose of incorporating Section 163-A of the Motor Vehicle Act, 1988 (pre-amendment i.e. 2019) was to provide a speedy remedy to the victims or their dependents.

And the compensation to be granted in case of death or permanent disability due to accident arising out of the use of motor vehicle under Section 163-A of the Motor Vehicle Act, 1988 (pre-amendment i.e.
2019)
is indicated in IInd Schedule of the Act whereby straight- jacket/structured formula has been applied as per the income, age of the victim only.

Further the claimant under this Section shall not be required to be pleaded or establish that the death or permanent disability was due to any wrongful act or neglect or default of the owner of the vehicle or vehicles concerned or any other person.
Section 140 of the Motor M.V.C.No.4003/2023 22 SCCH - 7 Vehicle Act, 1988 (pre-amendment i.e. 2019) lays down the liability to pay compensation in certain cases on the principle of no- fault.

And the amount of compensation in case of death of any person shall be fixed to the tune of Rs. 50,000/- and in respect of permanent disability of any person shall be fixed to the tune of Rs. 25,000/-.

This section also provides that the claimant shall not be required to plead and establish that the death or permanent disability in respect of which the claim has been made was due to any wrongful act, neglect or default of owner or owners of vehicle or vehicles concerned or of any other person.

28. As mentioned above in pre-amendment Motor Vehicles Act, there were two provisions regarding the grant of compensation to the victims/claimants i.e. Sections 140 and 163-A and now after the 2019 amendment the amount of compensation is also increased and by combining both the Sections i.e. Section 140 and 163-A, there is only one Section i.e. Section 164.
The Court should try to appreciate and see the intention of the legislation before deciding the cases.
The litigants place immense trust in the judicial system, viewing judges as symbols of justice.

Thus, judges have a duty to maintain this trust by delivering fair and substantive justice to M.V.C.No.4003/2023 23 SCCH - 7 the parties by actually and factually appreciating the evidence/conduct and over all facts and circumstances, difficulties faced by the near and dear ones, the gravity of loss, the gravity of agony and pain.

29. Now coming to matter on hand in view of the provision under Section 164 of the M.V Act (amended by the act 32 of 2019, the claimant shall not be required to plead or establish that the death or grievous hurt in respect of which the claim has been made, was due to any wrongful act or neglect or default of the owner of the vehicle or the vehicles concerned or of any other person.

In this matter the Petitioner sustained grievous injuries in the alleged accident due to involvement of the motor vehicles, hence in view of the above provision under Section 164 of MV Act the Petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.2,50,000/-.

Thus I conclude that, Respondent/RC owner of the unoffending Bus vehicle is directed to deposit the compensation amount along with interest at 6% p.a., from the date of filing of M.V.C.No.4003/2023 24 SCCH - 7 the claim petition.
Hence, I answer issues No.2 and 3 in the affirmative.
31. Issue No.4:
In view of the findings on the above issues, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER The claim petition filed by the Petitioner under Section 164 of the Motor Vehicles Act is hereby allowed with cost.
The Petitioner is entitled for total compensation amount of Rs.2,50,000/- (Rupees Two lakhs Fifty Thousand only) with interest @ 6% p.a., from the date of petition till its realization.
Further, Respondent being RC owner of the unoffending vehicle is directed to deposit the compensation amount together with 6% interest within 60 days from the date of this order.
After deposit, entire compensation amount with interest shall be released in favour of the Petitioner under E-payment with proper verification and identification.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw the award accordingly.

opennyai_summary.facts:
The petitioner filed this petition under Section 164 of Motor Vehicles Act 1989, seeking compensation of Rs.2,50,000/- for the injures sustained by him in the road traffic accident occurred on 26.12.2022.
2.
Accordingly, a case was registered in their Crime No.280/2022 and prepared F.I.R. for the offence punishable under sections 279 of IPC R/w section 129 R/w Sec. 177, Section 146 R/w Sec.196 of MV Act and submitted to the jurisdictional judicial magistrate and the superior officers and investigation was taken up by the investigating Officer.
opennyai_summary.issue:
M.V.C.No.4003/2023 5 SCCH - 7 :: I S S U E S ::
Dharanraj vs B.M.T.C on 8 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/112242500/
2 (1) Whether petitioner proves that the accident occurred due to rash and negligent act of driving of BMTC Bus bearing Reg. No.KA-53-F-0233 and as a result, he sustained injuries?
(2) Whether the Petitioner proves the age and earnings of the petitioner as stated in the claim petition?
(3) Whether petitioner is entitled for compensation?
If so, how much and from whom?
(4) What order or award?
opennyai_summary.arguments:
The Respondent admitted the alleged accident and its version is that, the alleged accident occurred due to the negligence and fault of the rider of the offending vehicle and no fault of the driver of the unoffending vehicle and therefore the driver of the unoffending vehicle cannot be held to be negligent and therefore the police have rightly filed Charge Sheet against the rider/ accused/ Petitioner of the offending vehicle.
21. The petitioner contended that as on the date of the accident he was aged about 25 years and he relied on the Ex.P.10/Driving licence of the Petitioner and wherein the date of birth of the Petitioner is shown as M.V.C.No.4003/2023 17 SCCH - 7 03.06.1997 and this accident was occurred on 26.12.2022.
The counsel for the Petitioner contended that in view of the claim petition filed under the provision of the MV Act question of negligence cannot be looked into and counsel for Respondent contended that no risk is contemplated under the insurance policy in respect of self negligent accident.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
. On going through the prosecution papers, FIR, Spot Mahazar, MVA Report, Wound Certificate,
Charge Sheet, and the evidence of PW-1 and RW-1 is specific to the effect that, the rider of the offending vehicle/accused is the reason for the said incident and at his instance, the incident took place.
The alleged accident was occurred due to rash and negligent riding of the offending vehicle and fault of the accused.
Therefore, considering the above discussed aspects collectively, it is the considered opinion of the Court that, the incident having been taken place in the manner asserted by the prosecution and the same being proved to have been taken place in the manner alleged by the prosecution, the accused drove the offending vehicle in a rash or negligent manner so as to endanger human life and at the spot dashed to the unoffending vehicle, as a result accused/ rider/Petitioner of the offending vehicle sustained grievous injuries in the alleged accident.
It is evident that injuries noted in the Ex.P5/Wound Certificate would be caused by a road traffic accident.
At the same time,
it has come out in evidence that the alleged accident was occurred due to rash and negligent riding of the offending vehicle and fault of the accused/rider.
Matters being so, the acts of the accused person clearly constitute the offences punishable under sections 279 of IPC R/w section 129 R/w Sec. 177, Section 146 R/w Sec.196 of MV Act.
Thus because of such negligent act of the accused/rider of the offending vehicle, it resulted in the injuries to himself, as the accused drove the said offending vehicle very rashly and negligently on the spot.
Therefore, the alleged accident occurred due to the fault of the accused/rider of the offending vehicle.
From the above discussion and going through the provision of the MV Act, it is clear that the grant of compensation under the provision of MV Act with respect to claim petition on the basis of structured formula is in the nature of a final award and the adjudication thereunder is required to be made without any requirement of any proof or negligence of the driver / owner of the vehicle(s) involved in the accident.
In fact as per the claim petition filed under the provision of the MV Act, to permit the insurer to raise the defence M.V.C.No.4003/2023 18 SCCH - 7 of negligence would be to bring a proceeding under 163- A (before amendment) / 164 (after amendment) with effect from 01.04.2022 of the MV Act at par with the proceeding under Section 166 of the Act which would not only be self contradictory but also defeat the very legislative intention.
Hence in view of the claim petition filed under the provision of MV Act the insurer cannot raise any defence or negligence on part of victim to counter a claim for compensation.
The statute has to be construed according to the intent of the makers and it is the duty of the Courts to interpret the statute in such a manner that the true intention of legislature is achieved.
Taking a purposive interpretation of Section 163-A of the Motor Vehicles Act (pre-amendment i.e 2019 amendment w.e.f 01.04.2022), the clear intention of the legislation was to come to the rescue of all those who in the absence of any evidence are not in a position to file a claim petition under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicle Act, where death of the victim or permanent disablement of the victim is required to be proved by establishing the factum of negligence involving the offending vehicle resulting into causing of accident, but under Section 163-A (pre- Dharanraj vs B.M.T.C on 8 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/112242500/
8 amendment i.e 2019 amendment w.e.f 01.04.2022) the M.V.C.No.4003/2023 21 SCCH - 7
requirement of proving the negligence was dispensed with.
The Court should try to appreciate and see the intention of the legislation before deciding the cases.
The litigants place immense trust in the judicial system, viewing judges as symbols of justice.
Thus, judges have a duty to maintain this trust by delivering fair and substantive justice to M.V.C.No.4003/2023 23 SCCH - 7 the parties by actually and factually appreciating the evidence/conduct and over all facts and circumstances, difficulties faced by the near and dear ones, the gravity of loss, the gravity of agony and pain.
In this matter the Petitioner sustained grievous injuries in the alleged accident due to involvement of the motor vehicles, hence in view of the above provision under Section 164 of MV Act the Petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.2,50,000/-.
opennyai_summary.decision:
29. Now coming to matter on hand in view of the provision under Section 164 of the M.V Act (amended by the act 32 of 2019, the claimant shall not be required to plead or establish that the death or grievous hurt in respect of which the claim has been made, was due to any wrongful act or neglect or default of the owner of the vehicle or the vehicles concerned or of any other person.
Hence, liability to pay the compensation amount is fixed on the respondent/RC owner and respondent is directed to deposit the compensation amount.
Thus I conclude that, Respondent/RC owner of the unoffending Bus vehicle is directed to deposit the compensation amount along with interest at 6% p.a., from the date of filing of M.V.C.No.4003/2023 24 SCCH - 7 the claim petition.
Hence, I answer issues No.2 and 3 in the affirmative.
31. Issue No.4:
In view of the findings on the above issues, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER The claim petition filed by the Petitioner under Section 164 of the Motor Vehicles Act is hereby allowed with cost.
The Petitioner is entitled for total compensation amount of Rs.2,50,000/- (Rupees Two lakhs Fifty Thousand only) with interest @ 6% p.a., from the date of petition till its realization.
Further, Respondent being RC owner of the unoffending vehicle is directed to deposit the compensation amount together with 6% interest within 60 days from the date of this order.
After deposit, entire compensation amount with interest shall be released in favour of the Petitioner under E-payment with proper verification and identification.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw the award accordingly.
